PullRequest.Title: Fix HydraFusion in tabbed model picker to remove chevron and add link
PullRequest.Body: This pull request addresses the rendering of the HydraFusion entry in the tabbed model picker by removing the chevron and displaying the description directly beneath the entry, similar to the Auto tiers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh the tabbed model picker in Copilot Auto mode when HydraFusion is available
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The UI thread rebuilds destinations and Auto-mode items, renders virtualized ActionList rows, constructs one Link for the HydraFusion detail in each instantiated active/sizing list, then performs the ActionList's existing width measurement and layout before the picker is usable.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total model rows controls the existing list build and width-measurement work; the diff's added link work has effective cardinality one HydraFusion row per instantiated Auto-mode list, independent of the number of ordinary models.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All item construction, DOM rendering, list splicing, width measurement, and layout are serialized on the UI thread; no new queue, burst, or asynchronous work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cache for rendered rows; refreshes recreate visible row state. Virtualized row reuse clears element disposables first, and the new detail-link registration is removed with that disposal. Cold and warm opens therefore each do bounded constant extra work for HydraFusion.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed item builder, renderer, disposal store, registration map, list refresh, and width measurement paths were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact list instantiation and browser layout duration depends on picker state and platform, but the changed work remains a single anchor/listener registration per HydraFusion row and replaces the prior expandable-hover metadata; it does not scale with the full model collection.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded DOM allocation and CSS layout for one row, removes the expandable hover construction path, and correctly disposes the Link and map entry when the virtualized row is rerendered or removed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate HydraFusion's Learn more link by pointer or keyboard
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user activation dispatches through Link to the picker linkHandler, then calls openerService.open for the external documentation URI; opening the URI is the only expensive boundary and is required before the scenario completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the external HydraFusion documentation URI through openerService, potentially delegating to the OS/default browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one call for each pointer, Enter, Space, or touch activation accepted by the Link control.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The expandable HydraFusion hover contained a Learn more link that ultimately invoked openerService for the same URI; the diff changes discoverability and placement, not boundary cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The boundary is the requested outcome of the click; it runs only after explicit activation and does not block picker rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One opener call per explicit user activation; there is no per-model or per-event fan-out after grouping.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each activation is handled independently on the UI event loop. The code does not add background concurrency, retries, batching, or speculative opens.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Cold and warm activations have the same one-call behavior, with no retained response or negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: Link activation, the supplied linkHandler, and its openerService call were traced end to end.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External browser launch latency varies by platform, but the diff neither adds the boundary nor increases calls per activation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The same user-triggered opener boundary remains one-for-one; it is not moved onto render, focus, hover, startup, or another hotter path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Generate Chat accessibility help containing the updated HydraFusion keyboard instruction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The help builder appends a localized static string while constructing the accessibility help text; no asynchronous or external work must complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per help invocation; the changed sentence does not depend on model count, history, or document size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-threaded string construction with no scheduling or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache behavior; the localized string follows the same lookup and append path as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete changed hunk is a one-for-one string replacement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; only static localized text content changed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and traced picker render/refresh, detail-link lifecycle and keyboard traversal, external-link activation, CSS layout, tests, and accessibility-help construction. No diff-caused hot-path, scaling, retention, boundary-fanout, or concurrency regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
